textbookText: c. Effects on human i. Smoke, fly ash, dust, soot etc. deteriorate the clothes and other articles used by human and also produce allergic reaction causing bronchial asthma, chronic bronchitis. ii. Carbon monoxide combines with haemoglobin to form carboxy-haemoglobin and stops the formation of oxy-haemoglobin which lead to serious health disorders like asphyxia, impairs O2 transport, headache and blurred vision. iii. Hydrogen sulphide causes eye and throat irritation and nausea. iv. Nickel and cadmium also cause respiratory disorder whereas metal like lead causes anaemia and nervous disorder. v. Oxides of nitrogen in air cause eye allergies, respiratory problems, dilation of arteries, lung oedema etc. vi. Various disease are increasing due to air pollution such as dementia, stroke, poor mental health, autism, COPD, lung cancer, asthma. Women may suffer from anaemia, infertility, miscarriage, gestational diabetes, premature menopause mental illness.
3. PREVENTIVE MEASURES i. Particulate pollutants in air can be separated and extracted by using some equipment like arresters and scrubbers.

ii. Pollutants released from industries should be changed into least toxic form by some chemical treatments before releasing to the environments. iii. No harmful gases and particulate matters are released by electric vehicles or automobiles. So, their uses should be highly prioritized by the government and public. iv. Least consumption of fossil fuels and excessive emphasis on the alternative sources of energy such as solar energy electricity biogas should be given. v. Industries should be open far from human settlement, public awareness, strict implementation of law or environmental act prevent air pollution.

Figure: 9.3.2 Instruments used in purifying air 9.3.3 WATER POLLUTION Water pollution is change in natural quality of water due to the addition of external substances or contaminants in it. It may also be defined as the degradation of the quality of water due to mixing of inorganic, organic, biological, radiological substance and heat. Such activity makes water unfit and unhealthy for human use and survival of aquatic life. In general, normal water is colourless, odourless, and tasteless but polluted water is turbid and having unpleasant smell and so does its taste. Any undesirable change in physical, chemical and biotic components of aquatic environment is called water pollution.
